title: Contextual SLO manifest: input-length & model-variant error budgets, failover triggers, and eviction rules
creator: Priya Shah
description: Define a canonical, per-endpoint and per-model SLO/SLI manifest that is aware of input context (notably input token length distributions) and model variant characteristics. Deliverable is a machine-readable SLO manifest spec plus human-runbook that: 1) expresses latency and availability SLIs per endpoint and model-variant, 2) defines error-budget accounting in both request-weighted and token-weighted terms, 3) specifies multi-region failover gates and automated eviction triggers, and 4) codifies circuit-breaker thresholds and hysteresis to feed the routing/orchestration layer. This ticket focuses on policy decisions, metric names/units, and a reference implementation in the servicing config repo. Implementation of enforcement and dashboards will be follow-up work assigned to the runtime observability squad.
acceptance_criteria: A machine-readable SLO manifest schema (JSON/YAML) that supports per-endpoint, per-model-variant, and input-length buckets

Definitions for primary SLIs: success_rate, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, p99_latency_ms, tail_latency_ms (99.9th), and normalized_quality_score; each with an exact metric name and aggregation window
Error budget accounting algorithm documented: request-weighted and token-weighted variants with examples for bursty routes
Explicit failover and eviction rules that map error-budget burn to actions: capacity preemption, variant fallback, regional failover; with thresholds and hysteresis
Circuit breaker spec: open/half-open/closed states, triggers for 5xx error rate and latency, minimum-open duration, and ramp-up backoff behavior
Runbook doc (Confluence link) and a staging dashboard in Grafana with examples for three representative endpoints
Design doc and a reference PR in serving-config that wires the manifest to the existing routing policy engine
notes: Motivation: single SLO format today is insufficient because latency and cost scale non-linearly with input token length and different model variants have divergent cost/latency trade-offs.
We want predictable developer-level SLAs: developers can pin an endpoint to a manifest row and reason about error budgets in units that reflect real cost (tokens) as well as UX (requests).
Trade-offs considered: token-weighted budgets better reflect cost but are harder for customer expectations; decided to support both and expose both on dashboards.
Scope exclusion: detailed autoscaler or broker enforcement code is out of scope for this ticket; those will consume the manifest via defined API in a follow-up ticket.
sli_definitions: success_rate: count(status in 2xx)/count(requests) over 1m, 5m, 1h windows; excludes client-abort errors per codebook
p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, p99_latency_ms: server-side end-to-end generation latency measured from request-received to final-token-emitted across non-streaming routes; aggregated per 1m and 5m
tail_latency_ms (99.9): used for safety gating on low-latency routes (e.g., interactive chat) with separate burn calculus
normalized_quality_score: sampled metric (0-1) derived from eval promptset checks; rolling 24h average used for quality SLOs and model-variant rollback triggers
token_consumption_per_request: tokens_generated + tokens_prompt; used to compute token-weighted error budget consumption
error_budget_policy: Request-weighted error budget: default 99.9% success over 30d measured in number of failed requests; suitable for control-plane and billing-sensitive customers
Token-weighted error budget: default 99.5% token-success over 30d where each failed request consumes tokens_generated + tokens_prompt; better aligns with cost-aware routing
Burn attribution: failures that occur while falling back to a cheaper variant count to the primary variant's budget unless request explicitly pinned
Rolling-window accounting: use sliding 30d window for long lived endpoints and 24h for canary experiments
Cross-region borrowing: allow a region to borrow up to 10% of another region's preserved budget under emergency failover; borrowing requires explicit arbiter approval (automatable later)
failover_and_eviction_rules: Failover gate 1 (regional): trigger when regional primary availability < 99.0% for 10m AND token-weighted burn-rate > 0.5% over 10m
Failover gate 2 (variant fallback): if primary variant p99_latency > SLO threshold for 5m AND quality_score within 2% of fallback, initiate soft-fallback to compatible variant

Eviction priority order: 1) ephemeral background batch jobs, 2) bronze routes, 3) silver routes, 4) pinned gold routes (pinned routes evicted only under regional evacuation emergency), 5) internal system traffic

Eviction behavior: when eviction invoked, start with preemptible pools, then instruct dedicated pools to free up lowest priority ASGs; inform console via event; 5m notice and progressive draining of sessions
Graceful rollback: any automated fallback must attempt a 1-minute hedged probe to validate compatibility before fully switching traffic
circuit_breaker_spec: Metrics that drive breakers: rolling 5m 5xx_rate, rolling 5m p99_latency relative to manifest threshold, and sudden spike in plugin errors
Open condition: 5xx_rate > 1.0% for 5m OR p99_latency > 3x SLO for 5m
Half-open probe: allow 1% of baseline QPS (min 5 rps) for 30s; if probes succeed, transition to closed with exponential backoff ramp-up
Hysteresis: after close, suppress breaker re-open for 15 minutes unless 5xx_rate remains > 2x threshold
Per-tenant soft-circuit: customers with reserved capacity may have relaxed thresholds (configurable per manifest row)
Telemetry: emit breaker state change events to Kafka topic infra.events.breakers and include salient metrics for debugging
observability_and_metrics: Canonical metric names: redwood.sli.success_rate, redwood.sli.latency.p99_ms, redwood.sli.token_consumption, redwood.sli.quality_score
Dashboard: staging Grafana dashboard created at https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/endpoint-resilience/contextual-slo-demo with example panels
Alerts: Pager alert if a manifest error-budget burn rate exceeds 5%/day for two consecutive days and for P0 endpoints immediate paged alert
Sampling: quality_score sampling at 1% of requests by default; configurable per-endpoint for high-sensitivity routes
implementation_plan: 1) Finalize SLO manifest JSON schema and publish to Confluence (owner: @Priya Shah)
2) Build reference parser and validator in serving-config (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-config/pull/12345)
3) Wire manifest consumer to routing/orchestrator (follow-up ENG ticket for enforcement)
4) Create Grafana dashboard and example manifests for 3 endpoints (chat-low-latency, batch-embeddings, reranker)
5) Run a 2-week shadow run where manifest-derived breakers are simulated and compared to current heuristics
